A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAT research and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–D. Content can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments on Relational Games, mathematical reasoning, CIFAR classification, and language modeling, including numerical comparisons and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experimental results and adds a qualitative analysis of learned visual relations in Appendix C.3.

M1.justification: The relational-attention operation, three symbol-assignment mechanisms, dual-attention heads, and encoder/decoder algorithms remain unchanged. Revised explanations and the new activation visualization do not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Relational Games and mathematical tasks, CIFAR-10/100, FineWeb-Edu, and TinyStories. The new visualization examines existing CIFAR coverage without introducing a distinct task or test environment.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Transformer/ViT baselines, PrediNet, CoRelNet, Abstractor, and RA-versus-RCA variants. The expanded citations do not introduce additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new Figure 9 introduces a qualitative inspection procedure comparing the first relation component at layers 1 and 5 for a selected CIFAR patch. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, model configurations, and quantitative metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a visual interpretability case study examining whether learned patch relations reflect visual similarity. Existing symmetry, augmentation, and RA-versus-RCA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-trial bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for Relational Games and mathematics, and ten-run mean/standard-error reporting for CIFAR comparisons. No statistical estimation or repeated-run reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds qualitative evidence of visual patch-similarity relations. Existing numerical results and plotted curves are unchanged: Table 1 retains CIFAR-10 accuracies of 86.4% for ViT and 89.7% for ViDAT, while Table 5 retains 350M-scale perplexities of 16.94 and 16.09.

T1.justification: The approximation theorem, continuity and uniqueness assumptions, Appendix A proof, and architectural algebra are retained. Removing the introductory generic message-passing illustration changes exposition rather than the theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: combining sensory and relational attention and demonstrating data and parameter efficiency across domains. Replacing the introduction’s contribution bullets with prose preserves their substantive claims.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3 and C.3 add an interpretation of source patches as filters and relation dimensions as convolution-like channels. The language-model interpretability discussion also adopts a more complementary framing toward existing attention studies. The substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 9 documents the visualization’s selected relation component, layers, tanh normalization, and activation-to-color mapping. Existing implementation details, training hyperparameters, tokenization, symbol choices, and advertised code/model access are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning through symbolic cognition, symbol grounding, and contemporary LLM reasoning literature, including chain-of-thought, emergent analogical reasoning, and GSM-Symbolic. It acknowledges reasoning acquired through large-scale training and drops the brain-workspace analogy. The detailed Abstractor comparison remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten, replacing message-passing exposition and contribution bullets with a historical and LLM-focused narrative. V3 also revises terminology and prose and adds an Impact Statement. It introduces an incorrect reference placing Algorithms 2–3 in Appendix B.

P2.justification: V3 adopts two-column main text and references, extensively resizes and relocates displays, condenses Table 1, and places Table 2 on a dedicated page. New Figure 9 is added; v2 Figures 9–11 become Figures 10–12 with unchanged graphics.

improvement.justification: The expanded research context clarifies the motivation, and the new CIFAR case study makes learned visual relations more concrete. These provide modest benefits while the method, theory, and quantitative evidence remain stable. A small navigation regression partly offsets the gains: Section 3.2 incorrectly locates Algorithms 2–3 in Appendix B.
